examples.title: Rewound speculative step
examples.description: A step that was speculatively executed and then unwound after a conflict. It renders struck-through and de-emphasized but stays inspectable, and announces its rewound state as text.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { RunStepTimeline } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import type { RunStepTimelineEntry } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const steps: RunStepTimelineEntry[] = [
    {
      id: 'read',
      label: 'Read current inventory',
      status: 'succeeded',
      duration: '2s',
    },
    {
      id: 'reserve',
      label: 'Reserve stock (speculative)',
      status: 'succeeded',
      rewound: true,
      duration: '1s',
      details: [
        {
          id: 'reason',
          label: 'Why it was unwound',
          type: 'text',
          content:
            'A concurrent order won the reservation. This speculative branch was rolled back before commit.',
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 'retry',
      label: 'Re-read inventory and reserve',
      status: 'running',
      progress: 30,
    },
  ];
</script>

examples.title: A run's story
examples.description: The narrative variant reads steps as what happened: a marker, a label with its time, one line of description, and a streaming note while output arrives.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { RunStepTimeline } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import type { RunStep } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const steps: RunStep[] = [
    {
      id: 'started',
      label: 'Started',
      status: 'recorded',
      time: '10:45:20 AM',
      description: 'You started Release notes from the run page',
    },
    {
      id: 'find',
      label: 'Step 1, Find the last release',
      status: 'succeeded',
      time: '+1.2 s',
      description: 'Found the last release, 1.4.2, on Oct 23',
    },
    {
      id: 'collect',
      label: 'Step 2, Collect merged changes',
      status: 'running',
      time: 'now',
      description: 'Reading merged pull requests from GitHub. Streaming, so this entry is partial and grows.',
      note: {
        title: 'Merged since Oct 23, so far',
        lines: [
          'Fixes the refund total when an order has a promo code',
          'Adds a staging check before releases go out',
        ],
        streaming: true,
      },
    },
    {
      id: 'draft',
      label: 'Step 3, Draft the notes',
      status: 'pending',
      description: 'Waits for step 2',
    },
    {
      id: 'approve',
      label: 'Step 4, Wait for approval',
      status: 'pending',
      description: 'Waits for step 3. Resumes on the signal `notes-approved`.',
    },
  ];
</script>

<RunStepTimeline {steps} variant="narrative" label="What happened" />

examples.title: What happened: finished runs
examples.description: A finished run told as a story: Started has a plain grey dot and the entries after it green checks, times sit at the end of each line, and "Used Lookup order lookup-order" shows the identifier small and monospaced. The three runs are a chat reply, a run a schedule started ("The Daily summary schedule started this run at 4:00 AM (9:00 AM UTC)"), and a refund that asked for approval and was approved.

examples.title: What happened: waiting and checking
examples.description: A run waiting for you draws an amber ring on "Asked a question" with "Waiting for your answer", and "Next steps" dashed ("Continue once you’ve answered"). A goal attempt that finished is checked against the goal’s check: its entries have no outcome yet, so they are plain grey dots, and the last entry, "Checking the result now", is a hollow in-progress ring.

examples.title: What happened: a canceled run
examples.description: A canceled run lists what it did. "Drafting the summary" was interrupted, so it is a neutral ring ("Interrupted while writing"), and the last entry, "Canceled", has a prohibition glyph: "The goal was stopped. Work already done is kept."
examples.code:

  import { RunStepTimeline } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

examples.title: What happened: a failed call and a denied approval
examples.description: A run that is Done keeps a failed tool call visible: its entry has a red mark and an open note, "This call failed", and the run still ends "Finished; one tool call failed". After a denied approval the entry reads Denied with a neutral dot, the note you typed shows as "Your note, …", and the run ends "Done, refund not issued".

examples.title: What happened: a long rail, collapsed
examples.description: A rail of eight or more entries shows the first three and the last three, with one row between reading "3 more calls" and a "Show all 9" action. Show all opens the middle in place. Failed and waiting entries are never collapsed.
